editorial:
Imagine taking your aging mother back to a place she used to live, only to find out the house is now a hotel and she is acting very strange. You get to follow an artist and her mom as they walk through these old halls, feeling like something is off. The vibe is quiet and a bit creepy, making you feel like you are spying on a private family fight. It is not a loud movie with big jumps, but it keeps you guessing about what is actually happening in their heads.

Tilda Swinton is amazing here because she plays two different roles, and you will love seeing how she changes her voice and look. The pacing is slow, which might bore some people, but it helps build the mystery. If you like stories that make you think and feel a bit uneasy, you should definitely give this a try. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, but if you really love the look of the film, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best quality.
endingExplained: You eventually find out that the mother and daughter are actually the same person at different ages. The movie is a dream or a memory where the daughter is imagining her older self. In the final scenes, the two versions of the woman face each other and accept their shared pain. It ends with them merging back into one person, showing that the daughter has finally processed her grief and her relationship with her own past.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological mysteries and great acting.
